review.summary: The release-readiness chunk delivers a genuinely qualified 0.2.3 candidate rather than a documented intention. The recorded attempt-3 evidence is the complete phase-24 command set (tools/review_phase.py:215 enforces equality with commands_for(24)): contract baseline and 27-case self-test, red_team_management.py --check --require-through-phase 24 --verify-package-receipts, a 495-test tools suite, 14 check-rust runs covering fmt/check/clippy -D warnings/test/doc across minimal/default/all/red-team/gateway/tracing/json-unification on MSRV 1.89.0 and 1.99.0, dependency audit, native exports, both clean release packages, live-evidence verification and check-access-release --phase 24 --version 0.2.3. Every check exits 0 with per-check source_unchanged and checkpoint bindings; none are unexecuted. The patch-level decision is backed by real old-consumer execution: management_consumers.py:66 requires the three current examples to equal bytes extracted from the verified published 0.2.2 registry archive plus the 565 KB native-probe consumer bound to the 0.2.2 receipt field, and check-management-package.py:137-155 requires each to have executed as an external crate against the extracted archive with command, cwd, feature set, hash and unique execution index bound, alongside the access-policy example and frozen probe. Live qualification is bounded and candid: schema-2 read-only receipt, transport allowlist restricted to one GET path with limit=1 (examples/live_qualification.rs:268-278), one verified method (OAuth), four 403 permission prerequisites, no mutations, and an explicit disclosure that the probed api.sase .../mgmt profile is not the unchanged SDK default; qualification.json and LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md record the same outcome, with a regression test binding the prose to the receipt. Changelog coverage matches the plan: schema-bound versus frozen-parity enum names, both Unknown-to-named-variant transitions, typed projections relocated out of extensions with precedence and lossless fallback, the narrowed DRAFT/ACTIVE status domain with all five affected legacy values and the unchanged-wire caveat, retained G10/G25 behavior, and live limitations. Release gating layers correctly (clean package wrapper, access-release candidate binding to an ancestor commit whose tree equals the reviewed fingerprint, prepublication readiness guard, registry verification requiring an accepted current-source phase-24 readiness review, delivery observer), and publication/tag/CI remain explicitly pending for the separate delivery chunk. Remaining issues are three low documentation/evidence-linkage nits; no blocker or high finding.

findings.description: The packaged README still says the archived receipt "does not qualify the current management changes; fresh live evidence belongs to release qualification", and only links the historical 0.2.2 receipt (line 92). The fresh read-only receipt now exists and is bound by contracts/live-evidence.json, so a reader of the published crate page can conclude no current live evidence was produced at all.
findings.required_fix: Name docs/checks/phase-24-live-attempt-02.json (or contracts/live-evidence.json) in README.md alongside the historical receipt and state the actual current outcome (OAuth verified, four target-list filter probes 403 permission-blocked), instead of describing fresh live evidence as still forthcoming.

findings.description: contractTests/contractEvidence for the Red Team target operations changed by management 0.86.0 (list at 21465, and likewise listAll, create, get, update, probe, updateProfile) reference only crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_resources_contracts.rs. None of the new suites (crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_contracts.rs, _fixtures.rs, _models.rs) appear anywhere in the file, so the matrix documented as the exhaustive per-method contract-verification source of truth (docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md:6-8, README.md:38) understates coverage for exactly the behavior this release adds. The evidence itself exists and is hash-bound in contracts/native-fixtures/red-team-management.json.
findings.required_fix: Add the new management contract/fixture test references to the affected operations' tests entries in contracts/native-operations.json (the source tools/qualification.py:147 reads) and regenerate contracts/qualification.json so the per-method matrix cites the suites that actually verify the 0.86.0 behavior.

findings.description: verify_offline_delivery's packaged-consumer expectation is `3 if version == '0.2.2' else 2`, and its example list omits red_team_management. For phase 24 the function is unreachable (line 107 skips it), but the constant is now wrong for 0.2.3: check-management-package.py binds six `run --locked --offline` consumer executions (four examples, the frozen probe and access policy). If this branch is ever enabled for a later release it will fail or under-assert while appearing authoritative.
findings.required_fix: Either make verify_offline_delivery derive its expected consumer count and example list from the schema-3 receipt bindings, or delete/clearly scope the function to the historical 0.2.1/0.2.2 proofs so it cannot be mistaken for the 0.2.3 contract.

limitations: Read-only tools only: I inspected recorded command output and receipts but could not execute any check, compile the crate, or recompute SHA256 digests. I could not independently confirm that the reviewed source fingerprint 726ed2c9… or the checks digest 4d8b9696… match the current tree; the review gate in tools/review_phase.py recomputes both when the record is created.

The clean-package archives, the registry archive and the live-run binary are outside the repository (.local/package-worktrees, .local/artifacts, external registration), so their contents are assessed only through the hash bindings recorded in the receipts and verifier source.

I did not read any credential or tenant-registration file, and did not read docs/checks/phase-24-private-material.json; the private-material conclusion rests on scripts/check-private-material.py logic plus the credential-free --check result.

generated.rs is 6.7 MB and schema_graph.json 2.2 MB; I verified selected declarations (the three new models, both appended union tails, branch ordering) rather than the whole corpus, relying on the compiler, generator --check runs and the independent fixture ledger for the remainder.

Live service behavior for the new management functionality remains unestablished: the only new-code probes returned HTTP 403, and the probed api.sase .../mgmt profile is neither the SDK default nor one of the six declared endpoint-profile constants. This is disclosed in the receipt, CHANGELOG and LIVE_ACCEPTANCE rather than hidden, but no reviewer action can substitute for the missing permission.
Registry publication, the annotated remote tag and terminal remote CI are not part of this chunk and are correctly absent; they belong to the pending delivery chunk and are not credited here.

Historical infrastructure outside this scoped change (phases 1-23 receipts, the frozen TypeScript baseline, Portkey and dataplane corpora) was not re-audited beyond the cumulative regressions executed in this gate.
